name: [[482,146,36]] prime-index cyclic generalized-bicycle code on Z_241

provenance.construction: Generalized bicycle (two-block cyclic) code on Z_241 with m=241 PRIME. H_X = [circ(a) | circ(b)], H_Z = [circ(b)^T | circ(a)^T] on n = 2m = 482 qubits. a and b are low-weight codewords of a cyclic divisor ideal <g>, g | x^241 - 1, where g is assembled in one step as a product over a chosen union of 2-cyclotomic cosets of Z_241 of total degree 72. This fixes k = 2 deg gcd(a, b, x^241 - 1) = 146 by design before any distance search, giving rate 0.303. a exponents = [0, 5, 14, 22, 31, 41, 78, 108, 145, 155, 164, 172, 181, 186] (weight 14); b exponents = [0, 1, 9, 10, 40, 51, 78, 94, 117, 134, 157, 173, 200, 211] (weight 14); max check weight 28. Design rationale: choosing m PRIME empties the shift-invariant (period) and coset-union subspaces of Z_m, because Z_m then has no proper nontrivial subgroup. On composite m those subspaces are where two-block cyclic codes carry their lightest logicals -- e.g. on a sibling code at m = 273 = 3*7*13 the period sector at t = 3 cut the honest distance from 48 to 36. Both a and b are mined light codewords of <g> rather than random multiples of g (random multiples give d = 4-7), and a == b draws are rejected since (u,u) is then automatically a logical and forces d = 2.
provenance.notes: Found by Jukebox-Autoresearch. Distance is a witness-backed UPPER bound (d <= 42), not exact. The bound was tightened from an initially staged 45 in three stages: (i) a Lee-Brickell search restricted to the four active 2-cyclotomic component subspaces (k = 146 = 2 + 3*48; 392 searches, ~4.1M subspace trials) found nothing below 44; (ii) Lee-Brickell on the full 314-dimensional kernel (60 runs) likewise found nothing below 44; (iii) witness-returning RIS run of 128M total trials (2M trials per configuration over 8 seeds x pair-depths {8,16,24,32} x both orientations) exhibited the weight-42 X-logical packaged here (seed 123457, pair_depth 24). No independent-mechanism cross-check was completed: the pinned BP+OSD decoder (decode/distance.py) exceeded the available budget at this size, so the corroboration is linear-algebraic only. Novelty vs the literature is UNVERIFIED; the construction is a generalized bicycle code, a well-mined family, and while no board entry has these parameters we have not searched the literature for an equivalent [[482,146]] code. No equivalence to an existing board entry is known: the gate reported no exact duplicate and no Weisfeiler-Leman-equivalent entry. Distance revised 2026-08-19 by GPU deep refutation with the board's standalone ris_gpu tool (verify/ris_gpu.cu, sqetch kernels by Muzhou Ma, MIT) on an NVIDIA L40S: a 1,000,000,000-trial random-ISD recovery ladder per side (seed 88000007) committed a weight-36 Z logical, re-verified on the CPU with the repo's GF(2) arithmetic and recorded here as the new Z witness. The same budget found no X logical lighter than weight 43, so the claimed dX<=42 stands. This tightens d<=42 to d<=36 and the score from 146*42^2/482 = 534.26 to 146*36^2/482 = 392.55. The distance remains a witness-backed upper bound, not an exact-distance claim. @yhu1996 constructed the code. Refutation credit and the search budget are recorded in witness_provenance on each corrected side (schema 0.2, issue #611); authorship is unchanged.
